title: Module quiz: The Claude Agent SDK

questions.stem: A team writes its services in Java and wants the same agent loop. What does the documentation offer?

options.text: A Java edition of the SDK, installed from Maven
options.says: Ruled out because the SDK is "programmable in Python and TypeScript", and there is no Java edition.

options.text: Run the CLI as a subprocess in headless mode with JSON output
options.says: The first page says the documentation's route for other languages is to run the CLI as a subprocess, with the `-p` flag and `--output-format json`.

options.text: Managed Agents, which expose the loop as a Java library
options.says: Ruled out because Managed Agents are "A hosted agent harness that runs the agent loop, with sessions in an Anthropic-managed cloud sandbox", and not a library.

options.text: The Client SDK's tool runner, which is the same loop as the Agent SDK
options.says: Ruled out because for the Client SDK "You write the tool loop yourself, or let the client SDK's beta tool runner drive it", which is not the Agent SDK's loop.

origin.section: Four ways to build an agent

questions.stem: In the example output a denied push appears as "Permission denied: Nothing is pushed from an agent". Which part is written by the example's own hook and not by the stand-in's code?

options.text: The words Permission denied, before the colon
options.says: Ruled out because "The prefix Permission denied: in front of it is the stand-in's wording and not the real binary's."

options.text: The whole line, from the first word to the last
options.says: Ruled out because part of the line, the reason, is "which is the text of your hook", so the line is not all the stand-in's.

options.text: The reason that follows the colon
options.says: The third page says the reason "is the text of your hook".

options.text: No part of the line, which is copied from the real binary
options.says: Ruled out because "It is not the real binary, and nothing here shows how the real binary words its messages or schedules its calls."

origin.section: The example: three kinds of callback in one run

questions.stem: An agent in production must not run unbounded. Which two limits does the SDK offer?

options.text: A cap on tokens for each message and a cap on wall-clock time
options.says: Ruled out because the two options are "Maximum tool-use round trips" and "Maximum cost before stopping", with no per-message token cap.

options.text: A cap on files read and a cap on files written
options.says: Ruled out because `max_turns` "counts tool-use turns only", and no file cap exists.

options.text: A cap on hooks and a cap on tools for each turn
options.says: Ruled out because without limits "the loop runs until Claude finishes on its own", and hooks and tools are not what the two options count.

options.text: A cap on tool-use turns and a cap on spend in dollars
options.says: The first page lists `max_turns` ("Maximum tool-use round trips") and `max_budget_usd` ("Maximum cost before stopping").

questions.stem: A CI job uses bypassPermissions and also lists Read in allowed_tools, hoping to keep the agent read-only. Which fix does the documentation give?

options.text: Nothing is needed, since the allowed list already limits the agent
options.says: Ruled out because "allowed_tools does not constrain bypassPermissions."

options.text: Block the unwanted ones with deny rules
options.says: The second page says "allowed_tools does not constrain bypassPermissions", and that the way to block specific tools in that mode is deny rules.

options.text: Move the list into the callback, which is consulted first
options.says: Ruled out because "Auto-approved tools never reach canUseTool", so the callback does not see them.

options.text: Switch to the default mode, which makes the list exclusive
options.says: Ruled out because "This does not restrict Claude to only these tools", in any mode.
